c.pop: 63,000 (Highland Council settlement estimate; ~70,000 in greater urban area)
c.tagline: Capital of the Highlands, where the River Ness meets the sea

card: Contactless and card payment are the norm almost everywhere, including buses and small cafes; cash is rarely needed but ATMs are widely available
rides: Local private-hire firms (Uber does not operate in Inverness)

taxi.color: No single livery — mix of black cabs and private-hire saloons/estates
taxi.fareNote: Fixed fares commonly quoted for the airport (~£25/$32) and Loch Ness day trips; book by phone as street hailing is limited

emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies, 111 for NHS non-emergency advice; Raigmore Hospital is the main hospital
emergency.note: 112 also reaches emergency services (EU-standard number, works throughout the UK)

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Compact, walkable city centre — most sights are within a 15-20 minute walk of each other, linked by footbridges over the River Ness and the pedestrian paths of the Ness Islands

safety.safety: Very safe overall — Inverness and the Highlands consistently rank among the lowest-crime areas in the UK
safety.crime: Violent crime is rare; petty theft is uncommon but standard caution is sensible in the city centre late at night around pubs on weekends

hood_landmark.Merkinch: Merkinch Local Nature Reserve & Carnarc Point
hood_landmark.Ballifeary: Ness Islands footbridges & Eden Court Theatre

hood_desc: The compact heart of Inverness on the east bank of the River Ness, packed with the castle, cathedral, Victorian Market arcades, and most restaurants, pubs and shops within easy walking distance.

A hillside Victorian and Edwardian conservation area just south of the centre, historically linked to the old castle lands, now a quiet, affluent residential neighborhood centred on a small crossroads of cafes and pubs.
A traditionally working-class district on a former island between the Caledonian Canal and the River Ness, with a strong community identity, riverside walks, and the Merkinch Local Nature Reserve.
A leafy riverside residential area on the west bank near the Ness Islands, home to Eden Court Theatre and several of the city's guesthouses in converted Victorian villas.
A hillside residential suburb south of the centre with woodland walks, mostly modern housing, and a handful of guesthouses popular with drivers arriving via the A9.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality.

transit.sys: Stagecoach Highlands city and regional buses (no rail metro or tram)
transit.hours: Roughly 06:00-23:30 on main routes, with a reduced Sunday timetable
transit.pay: Contactless card/phone tap, the Stagecoach app, or cash on board
transit.map: Stagecoach Highlands Inverness zone map covers the city and surrounding villages such as Culloden, Smithton and the airport
transit.note: The city centre is small enough to walk entirely; buses are mainly useful for outlying suburbs, the airport, and day trips to Loch Ness or Culloden

transport.air: Inverness Airport (INV) has direct flights from London (Heathrow, Gatwick, Luton), Amsterdam, Dublin, Belfast and other UK/European cities
transport.train: ScotRail direct trains from Edinburgh (~3.5 hrs), Glasgow (~3.25 hrs) and Aberdeen (~2 hrs); the Caledonian Sleeper runs overnight from London Euston
transport.bus: Scottish Citylink and Megabus coaches connect Inverness Bus Station with Edinburgh, Glasgow, Aberdeen and other Scottish cities
transport.ferry: No direct ferry into Inverness; nearest ferry terminals are Ullapool (to Stornoway, Isle of Lewis) and Scrabster (to Orkney), each about a 1-2 hour drive
transport.car: A9 from Perth/Edinburgh in the south, A96 from Aberdeen, A82 from Fort William and Glasgow along Loch Ness

airport.name: Inverness Airport
airport.distance: 9 miles (15 km) northeast of the city centre, at Dalcross
airport.transport: Stagecoach service 11/11A/11B, about 40 minutes, roughly $6 (£5); taxi about 20 minutes, roughly $32 (£25) for up to 4 passengers

net.m: Good 4G/5G coverage in Inverness itself; coverage gets patchy in rural Highland glens
net.w: Widely available in cafes, pubs, hotels and the public library
net.gb: Around $15-20 for a 15-20GB pay-as-you-go SIM bundle
net.fwn: Free wifi is standard with a purchase at cafes like Velocity Cafe and Black Isle Bar, plus free access at Inverness Public Library
net.ap: Buy a pay-as-you-go SIM (EE, Three or Vodafone) at a supermarket or the airport on arrival, or set up an eSIM before the trip

tip.s: Not obligatory for taxis or general services; rounding up or adding a small amount for good service is appreciated but not expected
tip.r: 10-12% for table service if not already added; always check the bill for an included 'service charge' before tipping again
